what_it_does: Machine-learning malware detectors are widely deployed to flag malicious software on Linux systems, but their robustness against deliberate evasion is not well understood. ELF (Executable and Linkable Format) files are the standard executable file format on Linux, similar to .exe files on Windows. This paper asks: can an attacker automatically mutate a real piece of malware so that it still runs and does damage, but no longer looks malicious to the detector? ADVeRL-ELF answers yes, using a reinforcement learning agent (a program that learns by trial and error, like a game player) that repeatedly tries inserting harmless filler instructions called no-ops (NOP — instructions that do nothing) into the executable. By placing these NOPs strategically, the agent changes the statistical fingerprint of the file enough to fool the detector while leaving the actual malicious logic intact. The goal is to expose weaknesses in current detectors so they can be hardened.
